# Disabling contact observations

`disabling.tsv` records original VIOLET, SKY, OLIVE, and GRAY branches inside private `Organism.touchEffects2`.
Two source runs and the bundled JAR produced identical bytes.
All four compiled helper classes match across backends.
The fixture contains 545 cases, 1,098 snapshots, 3,294 actor views, and 553 original calls.
Each actor view includes every 154-field organism observation.

## Comparison contract

The fixed ledger and typed inputs precede Rust replay.
Compare all nongeometric scalars, gases, statistics, ARGB, reactions, endpoints, bounds, identities, ordering, and RNG exactly.
Only organism `_m`, `_m1`, `_m2`, `_mass`, and `_I` retain the established geometry allowance.
For finite geometry, use `1e-10 * max(1, abs(expected))`.
Classify geometric NaN and signed infinity explicitly.
All other floating values retain their recorded raw Java bits.
Snapshot markers `P` declare ordering metadata.

Only organism `_world` and `_visibleWorld` receive collaborator exclusions.
Selection remains callback-routing metadata.
Every other observed field remains a comparison obligation.
G/N observations include every genome and gene field.
H observations preserve primary, infected, and saved whole-genome identities.
Statistics observations retain live genome identities.
The separate genetics fixture covers mutable per-Gene alias topology.

## Execution and isolation

Compile `tools/reference/DisablingOracle.java` against each pinned backend.
Run `biogenesis.DisablingOracle NEW_OUTPUT_DIRECTORY` with the exact isolated arguments in provenance.
The helper validates four explicit profile roots through `toRealPath` before simulation access.
It rejects existing output directories and uses `CREATE_NEW` for the fixture.
Six actual negative invocations cover omitted roots, an escaped preferences symlink, and existing-output preservation.
Positive processes use a 120-second bound.
Compilation uses a 60-second bound; negative invocations use 30 seconds.
The existing runner terminates each owned process group after every outcome.
No GUI, network service, world frame, or genesis runs.

The final capture remains under `.workflow-local/disabling-oracle-5dkjd5dq/`.
Exact argv, cwd, exit status, output, and process groups remain in `commands.json`.
Original hash, size, and mode checks cover all 74 reference files.
All 159 compiled reference classes and 33 prior TSV fixtures retain their hashes.

## Constructor inputs

Each case resets actual source defaults and records all 147 mutable primitive Utils settings.
Initial organism attempts are zero; oxygen is `1000`.
Mutation bounds are `0..10000`; meta mutation is zero.
GREEN weight is seven; other selectable weights are zero.
The real construction seed is `827364`.

Distinct supplied costs expose payer and ordered-payment differences.

| Setting | Ordinary supplied value |
| --- | ---: |
| VIOLET energy consumption | 0.125 |
| SKY energy consumption | 0.25 |
| OLIVE energy consumption | 0.375 |
| GRAY energy consumption | 0.5 |
| BLUE energy consumption | 0.75 |
| DODGE energy consumption | 1 |
| MAGENTA energy consumption | 1.25 |
| FALLOW energy consumption | 1.5 |
| MINT energy consumption | 1.75 |
| Organic obtained energy | 7 |

Every override appears in U before construction.
Selected restoration cases supply SKY cost `2000`, allowing failed shield payment without killing the peer.
Payment cases supply zero costs or raw oxygen, including negative, infinite, signed-zero, and NaN values.
These method inputs do not establish public settings acceptance.

The helper creates real `VisibleWorld(null)` and World objects.
It uses actual gas-add, Organism construction, paste, and `World.addOrganism` methods.
Peer, victim, and killer enter at `(1000,1000)`, `(3500,3500)`, and `(2000,2000)`.
Peer is selected before addition, avoiding MainWindow callback branches without substitutes.
Actor IDs begin `0`, `1`, and `2`.
All contact calls use distinct victim and killer objects.

Five supplied genome identities precede actor construction.
Ordinary g0 contains two genes with the labelled weapon color.
Ordinary g1 and g2 each contain one GREEN gene.
g3 and g4 are actual deep `GeneticCode.clone` results from g0.
Lengths begin at `12`; theta is `index * 0.25`.
Branches are zero for the first gene and `-1` thereafter.
Symmetry is one; mirror is zero.
Generation is `41`; clade is `root`.
Modifier integers begin at one; constructor booleans begin false.
Targeted g1 recipes supply multiple genes, passive movement, modified SKY, or spore modifiers `9` and `10`.
All actual recipe properties appear in initial G/N inputs.
No later observed snapshot supplies constructor state.

## Labelled state controls

Victim and killer start with energy `1000`, active/alive flags, and cleared relevant classification and defense flags.
Ordinary victim and killer plant flags are enabled after those explicit resets.
SKY actors receive version two; other actor SKY versions begin zero.
Both actors receive movement/react flags, frame-movement true, update marker seven, and extra-effects false.
These labelled cache sentinels distinguish source writes from retention without claiming normal frame reachability.
Temporary colors begin MAGENTA with zero frames.
Photosynthesis begins at `10`; photo coefficients are `index + 0.25`.
Victim and killer retain supplied infection g3 and saved g4 references until source methods change them.
All later controls appear before their K call.
Arrays must match actual segment counts.

The spin-overflow case changes two raw gene lengths after valid actor placement.
Its physical body retains the real initial geometry.
The original `segmentsCheckPlant` reads those labelled metadata edits and reports spin `-2`.
No huge-body placement claim follows from that case.

## Original operations and coverage

The helper verifies the actor's exact current ARGB before invoking original `touchEffects2` through reflection.
K labels identify VIOLET, SKY, OLIVE, or GRAY.
The peer role and both indices remain explicit inputs.
The wrapper implements no biological formulas.
Observation copies the real Java Random through serialization before peeking at its suffix.
Every recorded method leaves the real RNG unchanged.

VIOLET receives one complete 66-color palette, including all selectable colors, internal colors, and two unknown ARGB values.
SKY, OLIVE, and GRAY receive every immediate source peer-switch group through representative cases.
The source inventory contains 36 VIOLET, 16 SKY, 10 OLIVE, and 22 GRAY groups.
Targeted cases then vary distinct material gates.
This is feature coverage, without an exhaustive Boolean Cartesian-product claim.

VIOLET observations cover prefix dodge marking, actor classifications, active and dormant plant poisoning, and photo sentinel immunity.
They include JADE degradation without actor payment, check-plant recomputation, passive TEAL, and live mixed-body restoration.
BLUE retaliation, SKY shielding, OLIVE retaliation, healing defenses, experience ties, altruism, and infectious gates remain observable.
The repeated JADE case records JADE, DARKJADE, DARKGREEN, and GREENBROWN transitions through three original calls.

SKY observations cover both actor versions, peer versions, mobility/classification gates, dodge frames, and existing frozen guards.
They include ordered dual shielding, twelvefold peer payment, partial oxygen, and mixed-body freezing.
Dormant BLUE modifiers `9` and `10` cross the original threshold.
Dormant FRUIT/DARKFIRE cases distinguish spore versions `1`, `5`, and `6`.
JADE healing, altruism, MAGENTA defenses, BARK aging, FALLOW, SPIKE, and nonmatching ARGB groups remain separate.

OLIVE observations cover plant/infection/enhancement precedence and the actor-versus-peer payment order.
Dormant BLUE modifier `9` changes all BLUE segments; modifier `10` retains them.
They include SKY restoration, modified-SKY update retention, plant/nonplant breakage, FALLOW eligibility, and BARK activity gates.

GRAY observations cover immunity, surviving versus dying, direct healing defenses, experience ties, and inactive branches.
They include BLUE retaliation, SKY protection, OLIVE counterattacks, altruism, BARK aging, and common peer death.
The VIOLET survivor case observes the source's post-survival DARKFIRE assignment.
A real death wraps the killer counter from `2147483647` to `-2147483648`.
Repeated contact after death preserves the source's BROWN-case behavior.
Post-death clade edits expose live statistics genotype aliases.

Every branch also receives partial/full/empty payment inputs and strict common-death boundaries.
These include negative, signed-zero, infinite, and NaN inputs.
They are explicit source-state observations, with no new numerical tolerance.

## Preservation and limits

Two pre-replay candidates remain preserved with their actual source/source/JAR outputs and helper snapshots.
The first candidate received six additional source-outcome cases and live restoration controls.
The second received labelled cache sentinels before freeze.
Neither refinement used Rust expected values or followed a production mismatch.
Provenance records both supersessions and hashes.

This fixture establishes original method observations.
Rust parity requires a separate strict replay and review.
It does not establish collision discovery, contact scheduling, full-frame behavior, public settings, UI, or networking acceptance.
